notes: Pooled re-observation record for V2-080, which pays the representative Provider's live observation ONCE for every source change accumulated since the last one, and additionally proves that the corrected working directory reaches the real child. It amends nothing: the bytes of V2-017-provider-cost.json, V2-022-provider-cost.json, V2-063-provider-live-claude-refresh-cost.json and V2-075-provider-live-claude-rebind-cost.json stay unchanged, no earlier ledger is reused, no earlier record's thresholds are raised, and this record's accounting starts from an empty ledger of its own. Four measurements sized it. First, every earlier ledger was read and none of them halted on money: the four ledgers' settled actual_usd fields sum to 0.00 USD, because the contracted flat-rate subscription settles every invocation at zero, so the ONLY threshold that has ever bound is the invocation count and the monetary ceiling is a second, so-far-inert stop rather than the operative one. Second, V2-075's ledger stands at exactly 12 of 12 for a nine-subtest vertical slice, so it halted on the count with no headroom at all; borrowing it is impossible and repeating its ceiling would repeat the halt. Third, V2-022's dogfood exercise settled 23 of 24. Those two exercises are both inside this pooled observation, so the measured floor is 12 plus 23 equals 35 invocations before the working-directory proof is added at all. Fourth, the gap between subtest count and invocation count in every past observation is transient provider failure, which consumed between one and three invocations per observation and is not avoidable by design. max_invocations is therefore 48: the measured floor of 35, the working-directory proof, and roughly the observed retry rate as headroom. Thresholds here are runaway-detection stops, never billing ceilings; reaching one halts the exercise for inspection and is reported as neither a success nor a failure.

rollback.trigger: the ledger reaches max_invocations or max_total_cost_usd (runaway-detection stop), or a single settled invocation exceeds the 2.00 USD anomaly threshold and the ledger's halted flag is set
completion_conditions: no further claude invocations are made for this task without a new, freshly-approved provider-preflight record
the ledger's halted flag, once set, is cleared only by the owner issuing a new approved record, never by editing this record or the ledger file in place

reaching max_invocations or max_total_cost_usd stops the exercise for inspection and is reported as neither a success nor a failure; the limits in this record are never raised and this ledger is never re-initialised to reset the count

the observation commit is recorded and made unreachable-proof by a durable ref, because gate rule G6b measures the diff between that commit and the judging commit and an unreachable observation commit makes the intersection unmeasurable
the intersection between that diff and the published exercise file set is measured, not argued: an unmeasured intersection fails G6b

approval.approval_reference: owner instruction recorded in the coordinating session of 2026-08-25, transcribed by the coordinator; see ev-v2-055-standing-authorization
approval.scope: The owner authorises the Loop to invoke the contracted flat-rate Provider subscriptions on the owner's own machines with no per-invocation approval and no count or monetary ceiling, for the duration of the v2 work. Preflight limits stay in force only as runaway-detection thresholds; reaching one is a stop for inspection, never a success. Transcribed by the coordinator under the owner's instruction; ev-v2-055-standing-authorization holds the verbatim instruction and the limits of this record's machine check.
